verification.method: Re-implemented old and new _unlocal_date verbatim in node v24 and ran under TZ=UTC, Europe/Paris, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo, Pacific/Auckland, America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, America/Sao_Paulo, Pacific/Honolulu with (a) the ms-since-epoch value Python serializes for datetime.date(2019,9,20) and (b) the toDateString() string 'Mon Sep 16 2019' that _on_select stores.
verification.result: New code: string input correct in all 9 zones (old code was one day early in the four UTC+ zones -- the reported bug). Number input: old code correct in all 9 zones; new code one day EARLY in all four UTC- zones (Los_Angeles, New_York, Sao_Paulo, Honolulu) and correct in UTC and UTC+ zones.
verification.python_side: bokeh/core/json_encoder.py:186 routes datetime.date/datetime through convert_datetime_type; bokeh/util/serialization.py:183-184 converts a date to ms since epoch at 00:00 UTC (bokeh/util/tests/test_serialization.py:118 asserts date(2016,5,11) -> 1462924800000.0). So value/min_date/max_date reach the browser as UTC-midnight timestamps on initial render.

findings.title: Initial value/min/max now render one day early in UTC- zones
findings.why_it_matters: Every user whose browser runs west of UTC (all of the Americas) now sees the DatePicker open on the day before the date the Python model set, and min_date/max_date are likewise shifted one day early; before this change those users saw the correct date. The function receives two different encodings: on initial render `new Date(this.model.value)` is built from the millisecond timestamp Python serializes at 00:00 UTC, while after a pick it is built from the local-midnight string `toDateString()` stores. Subtracting the local offset turns the local-midnight string into UTC midnight (fixing the UTC+ bug) but pushes the already-UTC-midnight timestamp into the previous UTC day whenever the offset is positive. Branching on the encoding fixes both cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the calendar date from the encoding instead of shifting: in render() pass the raw model value, and implement `_unlocal_date(value: string | number): Date { const d = new Date(value); return typeof value === "number" ? new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate()) : new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate()) }`. Assumption: numbers only ever arrive as Python's UTC-midnight serialization and strings only as toDateString()/local-parsed forms; a date-only ISO string ('2019-09-20') is parsed as UTC by `new Date` and would need the UTC branch too if the project ever sends one.
evidence: bokeh/util/serialization.py:183-184 -- elif isinstance(obj, dt.date): return (dt.datetime(*obj.timetuple()[:6]) - DT_EPOCH).total_seconds() * 1000
node scratch under TZ=America/Los_Angeles: number(py date 2019-09-20) old=2019-09-20 new=2019-09-19 (WRONG); TZ=Europe/Paris: string('Mon Sep 16 2019') old=2019-09-15 (WRONG) new=2019-09-16

findings.title: New tests never assert the initially displayed date
findings.why_it_matters: The integration file added for this fix would stay green while the widget opens on the wrong day: test_basic only checks the label text, and the two other tests only check the input after a pick. The initial-render path (Python timestamp -> _unlocal_date -> Pikaday defaultDate) is exactly the path the rewritten function regresses in UTC- zones, and the pick-path assertion only distinguishes old from new behaviour when the browser runs in a UTC+ zone. Asserting the rendered input value on load gives the suite a check that fails in any zone where the initial date is shifted.
findings.suggested_fix: In test_basic, after the label assertion add: `el = page.driver.find_element_by_css_selector('.foo input'); assert el.get_attribute('value') == 'Fri Sep 20 2019'`. Note this assertion fails under the current diff when the browser runs in a UTC- zone, which is the regression it is meant to catch.
evidence: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:63-64 -- el = page.driver.find_element_by_css_selector('.bk-input'); assert el.get_attribute('value') == 'Mon Sep 16 2019' (only after the pick)

residual_risks: The timezone-dependence of the displayed date is not exercised by CI unless the Selenium browser runs under a non-UTC TZ; under TZ=UTC both the old and new code produce identical output for every input, so the suite as written cannot distinguish them.
testing_gaps: No test runs the DatePicker under a UTC- and a UTC+ browser timezone (e.g. parametrize TZ for the Selenium driver or add a bokehjs unit test of _unlocal_date with a stubbed getTimezoneOffset) for both the Python-serialized initial value and the toDateString() picked value.
